knowledge_fragments.content: Systemic symptoms and presence of syndromic symptoms of the 74 cases are summarized in Appendix S4. From these 74 cases, 17 died (23%) (range 3 days – 19 months; mean 158 days; median 60 days), with high individual mortality rates for OS (2/8; 35%), graft‐versus‐host disease (GvHD) (2/3; 67%), metabolic disorders (1/3; 33%), AEC syndrome (1/4; 25%) and NS (2/14; 18%). Complications described are septic shock, renal or hepatic failure, multi‐organ failure, secondary hemophagocytic syndrome, failure of the central nervous system, respiratory failure, malnutrition, anaemia, thrombocytopenia and extensive diarrhoea.

Salient findings: massive splenomegaly; significant respiratory compromise; abdominal compartment syndrome; respiratory compromise; bone marrow suppression; 70% ablation achieved; splenic size had decreased from 18 cm to 8 cm. Confirmed diagnosis: Gaucher disease. Differential diagnosis includes: Gaucher disease.

knowledge_fragments.content: Drug-induced hypersensitivity syndrome (DIHS) is a multi-organ disorder characterized by cutaneous disease, eosinophilia and multi-organ failure occurring within 8 weeks after the introduction of a drug. The original description involved aromatic anticonvulsants and was termed “anticonvulsant hypersensitivity syndrome.” Later the name “drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms” (DRESS) was coined but this has been replaced by DIHS.
knowledge_fragments.title: Drug allergy: causes and desensitization. > Role of Viruses

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: A 3-month-old female infant born at full term presented with red, scaly skin lesions on the face following exposure to sunlight at 4 weeks of age. At 2 months, she developed marble-like, slightly raised red and purple lesions on her limbs, which had a pattern similar to cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenita (CMTC).. Confirmed diagnosis: Neonatal Lupus. Differential diagnosis includes: Neonatal Lupus.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Neonatal Lupus

knowledge_fragments.content: Another important limitation of preclinical applications is the incomplete integration of pharmacokinetic (PK) and multi-organ factors. In vivo, cardiac drug responses are shaped by metabolism, systemic distribution, and off-target effects in the organs. To address this, multi-organ microphysiological systems (MPSs) have been developed, such as heart–liver co-culture platforms that combine hiPSC-derived cardiac tissues with liver organoids or liver-on-a-chip modules, to account for drug bioactivation and clearance. These systems can uncover cardiotoxic effects mediated by metabolites that would be missed in heart-only models. Nevertheless, constructing robust multi-organ platforms presents practical challenges, including the need to optimize tissue-specific media, match physiologically relevant flow rates and scale across organs, and enable inter-organ communication that accurately reflects human physiology. At present, no universally standardized “body-on-a-chip” platform exists, and many multi-organ systems remain bespoke, limiting their reproducibility and widespread adoption. Consequently, the routine integration of PK/pharmacodynamic considerations into in vitro cardiotoxicity
knowledge_fragments.title: Advanced in vitro cardiac models for drug evaluation: integration of organoids, engineered tissues, and microphysiological systems. > Challenges > Limitations in preclinical drug evaluation and safety testing

knowledge_fragments.content: Presentation: Sometimes when you hear hoof beats, it could be a zebra: consider the diagnosis of Fabry disease.. Salient findings: unexplained left ventricular hypertrophy; cryptogenic stroke; irreversible organ damage; multisystem dysfunction; renal impairment. Confirmed diagnosis: Fabry disease. Differential diagnosis includes: Fabry disease; lysosomal storage disorder; multi-system disease.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: Fabry disease

knowledge_fragments.content: Cardiotoxicity remains a major concern in drug development, particularly for compounds that do not primarily target the cardiovascular system. Accurate assessment of cardiotoxicity risk requires consideration of inter-organ interactions, such as the influence of hepatic metabolism on cardiac function, which are often overlooked in conventional monoculture-based in vitro systems. To address these limitations, multi-organ-on-a-chip (Multi-OoC) platforms have been developed to integrate multiple tissue types, thereby enabling the physiologically relevant evaluation of systemic drug responses in human-based models.
knowledge_fragments.title: Advanced in vitro cardiac models for drug evaluation: integration of organoids, engineered tissues, and microphysiological systems. > Applications > Cardiotoxicity evaluation and drug screening using multi-organ platforms

Salient findings: early-onset cataracts; cardiomyopathy; cerebellar ataxia; optic atrophy; cognitive impairment; myopathy; central nervous system. Confirmed diagnosis: alpha B-crystallinopathies. Differential diagnosis includes: alpha B-crystallinopathies.
knowledge_fragments.title: Case report: alpha B-crystallinopathies

knowledge_fragments.content: Despite organ-specific triggers and clinical presentations, pathological fibrosis exhibits remarkably shared underlying features (Figure 1). Understanding these commonalities is crucial for developing broadly applicable anti-fibrotic therapies.
